sources.entry: SiliconScope - Sudoless Apple Silicon system monitor (menu bar + dashboard) with first-class ANE, Media Engine and memory-bandwidth tracking plus an E/P-core breakdown — the chip-level signals Activity Monitor doesn't show. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/kennss/SiliconScope) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: SiliconScope
summary.one_liner: A sudoless macOS system monitor for Apple Silicon Macs that tracks Neural Engine, Media Engine, and unified-memory bandwidth, shown in a menu bar item and a full dashboard.
keywords: see what my mac is doing
use_cases: Check whether a local LLM is bandwidth-bound or compute-bound
Monitor Neural Engine and Media Engine activity during on-device AI or video work
Watch headless Macs and Linux GPU machines from one dashboard
Diagnose unified-memory bandwidth bottlenecks on Apple Silicon
Keep a live CPU/GPU/memory glance in the menu bar
summary.what_it_does: SiliconScope is a macOS monitor for Apple Silicon that reports chip-level signals such as Neural Engine (ANE) activity, Media Engine throughput, and unified-memory bandwidth split across CPU, GPU, Media, and ANE. It runs as a menu bar item showing live CPU, GPU, ANE, Media, memory bars and bandwidth, with a dropdown of 60-second trends, top processes, and a workload verdict. The full dashboard offers per-metric cards (CPU, GPU, Memory, Disks, Network, Sensors, Battery) that can be pinned to their own menu bar items. For local LLMs it gives a bandwidth-bound or compute-bound verdict against the chip's spec bandwidth and a tokens/sec and tokens-per-watt benchmark. Version 4.0 adds remote monitoring: a small agent on other machines (headless Macs, Linux/NVIDIA boxes) joins the dashboard over an encrypted, paired connection.
notable: Sudoless, offline design with no telemetry or outbound calls
Measures Neural Engine activity directly rather than inferring from power
Remote agent support for headless Macs and Linux GPU boxes in one dashboard (v4.0)
Developer-ID signed, Apple-notarized, self-updating; installable via Homebrew cask
caveats: Requires macOS 14+ on Apple Silicon for the Mac app
Remote Linux monitoring is limited to a GPU-centric view with VRAM holders and Ollama models
